Mr. Jitendra Chaudhary, Advocate for the petitioner.
Dr. Kartikey Hari Gupta, Advocate for the respondents.
2. A Division Bench of this Court decided Special Appeal No.499 of 2015 filed by petitioner vide judgment dated 10.08.2018.

Operative portion of the said judgment is reproduced below:
"
Learned counsel for respondent Nos.4 and 5 assures the Court that the land of the petitioner would not be utilized without paying the compensation to him.
No person can be deprived of his land, save in accordance with law, as per Article 300 A of the Constitution of India.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned order dated 17.08.2015 is set aside.

The respondent University is directed to give effect to the communication/letter dated 15.11.2007 within a period of eight weeks from today."
3.

Perusal of the judgment reveals that a direction was issued to H.N.B. Garhwal University to give effect to the communication/letter dated 15.11.2007, within a period of eight weeks from the date of judgment.
4. This Contempt Petition has been filed alleging wilful disobedience of the aforesaid judgment passed by Division Bench of this Court.

5. Grievance raised by the petitioner is that, despite the direction issued by Division Bench of this Court in Special Appeal No. 499 of 2015, the price of petitioner's land, which is in possession of the University, has not been paid to him.

Learned counsel for the University, however, submits that University has deposited the entire amount payable as price of the land, amounting to ` 19,47,500/-, with the District Magistrate, Pauri,
on 07.08.2020, however, the said amount was returned by District Magistrate on the ground that the land was not acquired by the University under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894,
therefore, District Magistrate cannot receive the payment.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner had purchased the land in question from father of one Mr. Umed Singh way back in the year 1962,
however, Mr. Umed Singh had raised a title dispute, which was decided in favour of 1979 and the judgment & decree passed by learned trial Court was affirmed right upto Hon'ble Supreme Court.
Thus, he submits that there is no dispute regarding title of the petitioner over the land in question.
He further submits that only objection, which is now being raised by the University for not paying price of land to the petitioner, is that petitioner's name is not recorded in revenue records.

He further submits that mutation of name in revenue records does not create title and the dispute has been settled in favour of the petitioner right upto Hon'ble Supreme Court, therefore, the University cannot now question the title of the petitioner.

8. Learned counsel for the University fairly submits that the University has no objection in paying the price of the land to the petitioner, provided he executes the sale deed in favour of the University.
9. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner will execute sale deed in favour of the University in respect of the land in question, within one month.

10. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the contempt petition is disposed of with a direction to University to pay price of the land, as mentioned in communication/letter dated 15.11.2007, to the petitioner at the time of execution of sale deed by petitioner in favour of the University.

(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 14.07.2023 Arpan CLCON/452/2019 on 14 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159149205/
